fichas.title: Detached, one-family house
fichas.summary: An adaptation of the middle-class house for private house building on new estates. The plan may be rotated to place the entrance at the side; a driveway may provide garage access. The house receives light on all sides, and its rational layout includes a common area with kitchen and a central hallway. Nearby houses can limit semi-public outdoor space.

fichas.title: Terraced house and gallery access
fichas.summary: Terraced houses may be planned to evoke the spatial repertoire of a detached house. Row building limits direct lighting to two façades, and the text describes a potentially poorly lit middle zone. Intruding communal areas receiving daylight from both façades can help address this. An access gallery can transfer the terraced-house idea to blocks of flats, but may reduce lighting and possible flat depth; transverse stairs are common in two-storey plans.

fichas.title: Staggered and angled terraced houses; patio house
fichas.summary: On more generous plots, angled or staggered terraces can create protected private and semi-public outdoor areas while retaining similar plan areas and room layouts. This can be achieved by moving plan areas together or apart. Internal rooms can face the resulting patio areas.
